author: Tavmania
body:
Fellow Blademaster/Hunter here. Long post incoming.   

Initially, before I hit level 150, I came back often to the Majestic class because I couldn't find enough berserked enemies to take the full advantage of the Crest of Avalon buff. It turns out that this class doesn't just benefit from Berserk enemies but also *Arisen* enemies: they start spawning at level 150, T7. It makes it so that Crest of Avalon becomes much more reliable than Eternal Light of the Majestic.  

And Secone Chance is a ridiculous clutch mechanic. It might not trigger when you need it to. It sometimes triggers 4 times in a row. I personally appreciated it the most against the arisen monsters, especially before I get that Crest of Avalon buff up to 100%.  

I suspect that my skill setup is not ideal yet, but here's mine for the overworld:   


* Tri-cut II. It just has the highest multiplier and therefore, becomes your bread and butter for 0HKO-ing nearly everything.  
* Omni-Strike-II. If you purely followed the Rogue class without deviating, you will find that you don't have many reliable skills to stick into **7** skill slots only. Therefore, this is the only skill that triggers Attack, Magic and Defense debuffs into one slot.  
* Full Bend - why would I bring this it I already have Omnistrike? Because FB is a guaranteed crit AND lands a guaranteed Defense debuff on the enemy. Especially against Berserked/Arisen enemies, you will find that Tri-cut II is not enough by itself. Therefore, FB is king.  
  * I have considered Flurry-II, but I highly dislike relying on a % chance of an ailment/debuff proccing. It's why nobody uses arrows nowadays. Your Leaderboards may frequently show end-game rogues simply sticking to a (Masterforged) Whisper, it just works so well.  
  * People may disagree about the usefulness of the Hunter Specialization, saying that FB is not enough of a redeeming factor. Understandable, because Inquisitor and Berserker are considered the most popular physical specs. I simply find it the most fun.  
* Dragonslayer - (100 mana) why such an expensive skill? Dragons run rampant and this skill demolishes any of them. With some proper set-up, even Tiamat takes ~5k damage. Also, Dragon-element attacks are quite useful to take down Mimics, as they are immune to many elements including the physical element. The Dragon element seems to often bypass these immunities/resistances, making it a great back-up plan (Especially in Gauntlets!).  
* Barrier-II. Why bring a skill that brings ordinary buffs that come from low-tier potions? Because it's one turn for 2 buffs, and you don't have an eternity to set-up against dangerous bosses. I skip this skill in Gauntlet and use potions instead, bringing another skill purely for coverage.  
* Magic Shield-II. I bought the Sorceror class for this one and it was well worth the investment, especially because the T7 gear you will encounter often lacks resistance.  

Your 7th slot is more of a flavour thing. I use Swordplay against Starlord even though it usurps huge amounts of mana, but it actually makes me deal about 5k damage/90 mana whenever I simultaneously proc T.Attack up and T.Defense-down on Starlord. It helps to survive Quasar more easily too when you procc just right.  

>another example, in raids, Titans and balor elite destroy me, i can barely tank them and damage wise its like im tickling them!  

They have their gimmicks. Basically:  

* Titan has earth-elemental magic, making an Earth-resist accessory nice if you don't have armor that resist Earth. The rest of his skills are Physical. Balor has Fireball and uses other physical attacks, making a Flame Belt a good option.  

* You'll want Protection-II from the Centurion (?) class against these 2, to survive their ultimate skills. You should know about Ults, since you don't seem to have trouble with Starlord.  

* When it comes to offense, patience is key. You're not going to deal huge amounts of damage against Titan before his gear becomes uninteresting (unfortunately). Consider upgrading your pet as well (Wisp/Twilight Wisp), and start saving up that Orn for the next class! It makes one heck of a difference, even though it may not look like it due to the steep cost.  

> Am i missing something here or are mages better in general?  

It really does seem like they are better in general... Which is a shame. But it gets posted so often on this sub, physical might get a buff if this becomes repetitive enough?

author: [deleted]
body: From what I have seen and heard, the stat boost from the previous classes to Blademaster isn't great, so they may not hit hard. However, I think their abilities are supposed to make up for it. Second Chance, for example, just seems broken to me. The number of dukedoms I've failed to claim because Second Chance kicks in 2 or 3 times in a row, leaving them with 1 HP until I die, is ridiculous. That's all I can think of.

author: Drockvaen
body: Hi, I'm currently a Majestic about to class up to Blademaster, so your post interested me. I don't know how well this would scale up, but I've been using the mess out of Arrowstorm from Hunter. Been very effective so far. May even stick with this spec until Tier 9.
